tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

pfg-scheduling-constraints: Page 1, paras 5-6: the case story's own description of the scheduling problem and its constraints (store reach, drivers per shift, 10 h between shifts); the complexity remark is a plain statement of problem size
pfg-scheduling-goal-flexibility: Page 1, para 7: states the auto-scheduler's own goal (weekly assignments under user constraints, as many or as few shifts as each member wishes); a stated aim, not a result
platform-all-passive-lnoi: Sec 1, p.1: the paper states what it reports, an all-passive anti-PT realization on thin-film LNOI with three waveguides; device built from engineered coupling and loss as in Sec 2
device-geometry-waveguides: Sec 2, p.1: states the Z-cut LNOI stack and measured top widths 870/820/870 nm, heights 400 nm
device-gap-trench-fig1: Fig. 1 caption, p.1: states top gap about 820 nm and trench 1.9 um wide, 690 nm thick; the 690 nm depth agrees with Supplement Sec 1
coupled-mode-equations-and-detuning-defi: Sec 2, Eq. (1), p.1: the paper states the model and defines a_m, kappa and gamma. The equations follow Ref [26] but the symbols are defined here; no derived result is claimed
detuning-definitions: Sec 2, p.1 and Supp Eq. S2 text: the paper defines the two detunings from the propagation constants (subscripts lost in the text layer; Supp states Delta = k1 - k3 as the effective detuning)
microheaters-and-tm-mode-design: Sec 2, p.2: states the heater position (1.5 um above waveguides 1 and 3), TM mode choice and the trench; these are the paper's own design choices. The rationale clauses are the authors' stated design reasons
measurement-setup-1550nm-tm-waveguide3: Sec 3, p.3 and Supp Fig S2 text: states 1550 nm TM input into waveguide 3 via objective lens, lensed-fiber collection, power meter, 10 dBm input
mzi-imbalanced-phase-sweep: Sec 3, p.4: states the imbalanced MZI with dL = 435 um and the wavelength sweep 1544-1550 nm giving about 16 rad of theta; protocol of the paper's own phase sweep
baseline-detuning-undeterminable: Sec 3, p.4: states the fitting protocol, baseline Delta is the only fit parameter because it is extremely sensitive to the cross section and cannot otherwise be determined; the paper's own fit procedure and a stated limit
fabrication-flow-materials: Supp Sec 1, p.1: states the wafer, 20 nm Cr strip, 1.4 um oxide cladding, 690 nm trench depth, 30 nm Cr plus 100 nm Au heaters; all appear in the recipe text
coupled-region-length-and-heater: Supp text after Eq. S3 (L = 0.1 cm) and Fig. S1 caption (microheater 1 mm): device parameters stated by the paper
device-geometry-and-poling: Sec II, p.2: states the 8 mm PPLN nanowaveguide on 500 nm X-cut MgO:LN, 1.8 um top width, 2.5 um poling period, stage at 48 +/- 0.1 deg
conversion-efficiency-fit-model: Sec II, Eq. (1), p.2: the paper defines the fit model and each symbol (eta, eta_max, P, L); the text layer drops the radical but the form is the cited fit of Ref [21]. A fit model, not a claimed result
conversion-sweep-conditions: Sec II, p.2: states signal fixed at the SFG peak at 214 uW and pump swept 62 to 1230 mW
noise-measurement-pump-and-signal: Secs II and II.A, pp.2-3: states the 1559.7 nm CW laser carved to a 10 MHz, 10 ns pulse train by an EOM, and signal tuned around 1540.5 nm for the thermal effect
detectors-and-filter-rejection: Sec II.A, pp.2-3: states the ID100 at 15 percent, two 3 nm band-pass filters rejecting SH at 779.9 nm by over 120 dB, and SNSPD at about 85 percent
noise-filters-placed-off-signal: Sec II.A, p.2: states the measurement design, noise counted at 1551.7 and 1567.7 nm and not at 1540.5 nm, with the stated reason
coupling-loss-and-transmission: Sec II.A, p.3: states the 20.9 and 19.4 dB total loss, the 4 dB input coupling estimate (from a similar waveguide, as the value says) and eta1, eta2
four-signal-band-noise-mechanisms: Sec II.A, p.3: the paper states the four mechanisms its analysis covers (SHG-SPDC, SRS in fiber and waveguide, SFWM); the list is its own analysis scope
flat-spdc-gain-assumption-11nm: Sec II.A, p.3: states its assumption of a flat SPDC gain over 11 nm and that Eq. (3) holds only when pair generation dominates; the CAR check follows in the text
raman-spectrum-measurement-setup: Sec II.C, p.5: states the 10 MHz, 10 ns pump at 1537.5 nm and filter sweep 1550 to 1605 nm in 1 nm steps
time-frequency-mode-definition: Sec III, p.5: the paper defines a time-frequency mode and states the count BT for each pump pulse
detection-mode-counts: Sec III, p.5: states the mode counts 750, 1.5e4 and 5600 from B and T=10 ns used to normalize its noise; B values check against the stated filters
scope-10mhz-single-device: Sec I, pp.1-2: states noise is measured versus pump power at 10 MHz repetition rate, for telecom C-band to about 780 nm in an X-cut PPLN nanowaveguide
hypergraph-def: Definition 2.6 (Sec 2.2, p.6) and Sec 1.1: the paper defines a directed hypergraph and allows empty sets and multi-edges
aut-plus-def: Definition 3.5 (Sec 3.2, p.15), restated as Definition 1 on p.2: universal C*-algebra with two magic unitaries and relations AsuE = uVAs, AruE = uVAr
classical-case: Sec 1.1 states it and Sec 3.1 proves the ingredients: Prop 3.3 and Prop 3.4 (with proofs) show the intertwiner relations on permutation matrices are exactly the classical compatibility conditions of Def 3.1. Prop 3.9 also proves Spec equals Aut. The statement itself is not numbered but is a direct consequence of the proved Props 3.3-3.4
prop-3-9: Prop 3.9, Sec 3.2, pp.17-18: stated and proved; the proof uses Prop 3.4 and a standard cited fact on Spec of a Hopf C*-algebra (Ref [28])
prop-3-10: Prop 3.10, Sec 3.3, p.18: stated and proved by the universal property and a surjective morphism
prop-3-12: Def 3.11 and Prop 3.12, Sec 3.3, pp.18-19: stated for all n, m with s(e) = r(e) = V, and proved by constructing the inverse map
prop-3-14: Prop 3.14, Sec 3.4, pp.19-20: stated and proved (incidence matrices swap, so relations coincide)
prop-3-16: Prop 3.16, Sec 3.4, pp.20-21: stated and proved via Prop 2.24 and the universal properties
cor-3-20: Thm 3.19 (proved with Lemmas 3.17-3.18, pp.21-23) and Cor 3.20 (proved, p.23): condition is a hypergraph without multi-edges
cor-3-21: Cor 3.21, p.23: stated and proved by combining the dual statement (Prop 3.16) with Cor 3.20; condition is that the dual has no multi-edges
prop-4-6: Prop 4.6, Sec 4.2, p.30: stated and proved. The text layer drops the not-equal sign in 'Ns(v) = Ns(w) implies uvw = 0' (the proof gives (Ns(v)-Ns(w)) uvw = 0), so the value's 'differs' is correct but the quote reads wrongly
hyp-cstar-def: Def 2.34, Sec 2.5, pp.13-14: the paper states the hypergraph C*-algebra (introduced by Ref [29]). The reduction to the graph C*-algebra is only asserted, evident by comparing Defs 2.32 and 2.34, not proved
lemma-5-2: Lemma 5.2, Sec 5.1, pp.39-41: stated and proved, checking each relation of Def 2.34 using Prop 5.1 and Remark 3.6
thm-5-3: Thm 5.3, Sec 5.1, pp.41-42: stated and proved (action axioms and faithfulness)
magic-unitary-def: Def 2.21, Sec 2.3, p.10 and Intro p.1: the paper defines magic unitary (projections, rows and columns sum to 1) and notes complex ones are permutation matrices
open-q-complete: Def 6.1 and Question 6.2, Sec 6, p.46: the paper states it does not know whether Aut+ of the complete hypergraph is a proper subgroup of S_V+ (which holds as a subgroup by Cor 3.20, as it has no multi-edges)
open-q-graph: Question 6.3, Sec 6, p.46: the paper poses as open whether every hypergraph quantum automorphism group arises from a larger classical graph (the text says 'might be possible')
open-q-banica: Question 6.4, Sec 6, p.47: the paper states as open whether a Banica version exists
open-q-hahn: Question 6.5, Sec 6, p.47: the paper poses as open whether Hahn's results generalize with Bichon's free wreath product
garikapati-selectivity-definition: Model, Eq. 1, p.4: the paper defines selectivity S in dB as 10 log10 of desired-mode SF photons over the other considered modes, measured with the Si-APD (formula garbled in the text layer but its words match)
garikapati-mode-set-and-scheme: Model, pp.4-5: states 3 HG temporal and 5 LG spatial modes (15), a unique ST pump profile per mode, and monitoring of 225 pump-signal pairs
garikapati-pso-optimization-setup: Model, Eq. 2, pp.5-6: states PSO of the relative phase of 37 comb lines on 16 candidates, and use of the same technique to simulate the pump shape for the experiment
garikapati-experimental-setup: Experimental setup, p.7: states the 25 GHz comb, waveshaper pump at 1551 nm and signal at 1559 nm, SLMs, 5 mol.% MgO PPLN of 1 cm and 2.5 cm, SMF coupling, ID100 detection
garikapati-mub-definition: Results, Eqs. 3-4, p.11: the paper defines T+ and T- as normalized sum and difference of T0 and T1
garikapati-comb-line-limit: Discussion, p.14: the authors state their technical limitation, 25 GHz comb spacing gives about 8 lines in the 3 dB band of a 2 ps pulse, inadequate for modes above third order
garikapati-spatial-smf-coupling-limit: Discussion, p.14: the authors state that higher-order OAM modes give low counts through the single-mode fiber and that few-mode fiber would compromise spatial selectivity
garikapati-waveshaper-jitter-and-speed: Discussion, pp.14-15: the authors state the 2 ps jitter on waveshaper refresh, the delay-scan workaround, and the roughly 1 s per pair, a hindrance to adaptive optimization
garikapati-no-closed-loop-or-noise-test: Conclusion, p.16: extension to noisy environments (turbulence, time-frequency noise) is stated as future work. The clause that the results include no such noise is an inference, consistent with the Discussion and the experiments described

theory_low.anti-pt-condition-large-dissipation: a design condition (gamma much larger than |Delta| and |kappa|) taken from the model of Ref [26] and used for adiabatic elimination; it is not a stated limitation of the paper's work and is not proved here
theory_low.adiabatic-elimination-effective-hamilton: adiabatic elimination is applied and the result Heff and Gamma = |kappa|^2/gamma are stated without derivation in the paper or Supplement; a theoretical result not proved in this paper
theory_low.heff-anticommutes-with-pt: the anticommutation is asserted in one line with no calculation shown; a theoretical statement not proved in the paper
theory_low.eigenvalues-anti-pt-phase: Eq. (4) is stated without derivation; Supplement says eigenvalues are 'solved following Ref. [3]'. Not proved in this paper
theory_low.eigenstates-equal-amplitude-anti-pt-phas: Eq. (5) is stated without derivation or orthogonality proof; not proved in this paper
theory_low.zero-detuning-one-lossless-eigenstate: follows from Eqs. (4)-(5) but is stated without derivation; the text is also partly garbled in the layer. A theoretical statement, not proved here
theory_low.equal-splitting-robustness-claim: the robustness is the authors' inference from the eigenstate structure; no derivation of tolerance. Only the measured flat splitting (Fig. 2b) and a simulation (Fig. S5) back it, both results
theory_low.broken-phase-eigenvalues-states: Eqs. (6)-(7) and the asymmetry statement are given without derivation, and nonreciprocity is cited to Ref [26]; not proved in this paper
theory_low.hermitian-sim-3db-needs-10nm: a simulation outcome (Supp Fig. S5) for a comparison structure, a computed result, not a setup or proof
theory_low.direct-raman-of-residual-sh-overestimate: Eqs. (4)-(5) are a short model calculation: it assumes an undepleted pump and quadratic growth of SH along the guide, and the quotes drop these conditions. A modeled estimate, not a theorem
theory_low.table1-projected-configurations: Table I rows other than the first are projections of noise under changed configurations, computed estimates from the measured contributions; values match the table
theory_low.thm-4-3: cross-group consistency, Rule A (coordinator, 2026-10-30): Theorem 4.3, Sec. 4.1, pp.26-27: the magic-unitary step for uE uses 'the additional relations from Proposition 2.29', which is derived from Proposition 2.28, whose proof is only 'See [25, Proposition 2.1.3.]' (p.12): a cited result, not proved in this paper.
theory_low.thm-4-7: cross-group consistency, Rule A (coordinator, 2026-10-30): Theorem 4.7, Sec. 4.2, pp.30-33: the row and column sums of uE are obtained 'by Proposition 2.29' (p.31), which rests on Proposition 2.28, proved only by 'See [25, Proposition 2.1.3.]' (p.12), a cited result.
theory_low.thm-4-11: cross-group consistency, Rule A (coordinator, 2026-10-30): Theorem 4.11, Sec. 4.3, pp.36-38: uV is a magic unitary by Lemma 4.10, whose proof uses 'an argument from the proof of [31, Theorem 3.1]' and '[33, Proposition 3.2]' (Woronowicz) to get left-invertibility (p.35); both are cited results, not proved here.
theory_low.thm-5-8: cross-group consistency, Rule A (coordinator, 2026-10-30): Theorem 5.8, Sec. 5.2, pp.45-46: the proof uses Lemma 5.7, whose first part is 'contained in the proof of [31, Theorem 3.1]' (p.44), a cited result not reproduced in this paper.
theory_low.lemma-5-7: only part of the lemma is proved here: the proof that uV is a magic unitary is 'contained in the proof of [31, Theorem 3.1]' (Wang), cited and not reproduced. The second part (AruE = uVAr) is proved in the paper. Split the claim if the second part is wanted as HIGH
